pairs.subject: scoring-rubrics
pairs.evidence: features/civicscore/components/HeadToHead.tsx:245 The Souboj breakdown reads each component as a plain number (Record<ComponentKey, number>, no absent state) and draws it as a bar, so a dimension that was never measured shows up as a zero-height bar with no coverage note. The fact rows below it do keep missing distinct from zero, so the honesty is only half there.

techniques.evidence: features/civicscore/components/HeadToHead.tsx:256 The component bar is drawn straight from earned points. The rubric's own declaration (lib/analysis/contribution.ts:16-17) says missing dimensions 'simply contribute 0', so an absent dimension renders as an empty bar instead of a 'not measured' row, and the breakdown states no coverage. The fact layer, by contrast, is conformant: duelFacts.ts:69 treats null as no comparison.

features/civicscore/components/HeadToHead.tsx:278 The composite renders with its per-component contributions and each weight, and the composite's citation comes from the shared scoreClaim minter rather than a re-derivation. No top gap is phrased as an action, but this is a comparison surface.

features/civicscore/provenance.ts:133 The stored scores carry a formula ref plus a pass number. The aggregate compares those against the ref the code declares and surfaces a mismatch or a mixed store (MetodikaPage storeMismatch), and provenance.test.ts pins the match, mismatch, mixed and absent cases.

features/civicscore/MetodikaPage.tsx:47 The page imports the single weight vector and computes its total instead of writing it as a literal; the sum of 100 is asserted in componentDefs.test.ts. Caveat: the declaration off-context gives no per-weight rationale (only 2 of 6 weights have comments, and those describe what the weight counts, not why).
features/civicscore/MetodikaPage.tsx:135 The fixed saturation anchors (the frame) are published from imports. Not done: the duel breakdown never says when a dimension is clamped at its cap.

features/civicscore/components/HeadToHead.tsx:177 The 'lens' here is a weight vector the reader chooses, not one selected by population; there is no population classifier. A custom lens is labelled (cobalt colour) and its citation is withheld.
features/civicscore/duel.ts:12 The context compares two MPs and explains the formula; no work queue consumes a ranked gap list. Tie handling (duelOutcome at published precision) is deterministic.
